PART 1How to use this document

For Claude design module: Each spec has an "OPEN FOR DESIGN REVIEW" block at the bottom. Refine copy, propose alternative layouts, push back on flows, surface design system inconsistencies. The structured format makes inline review easy — comment per section.
For Codex: Each spec has FILES (real repo paths), COMPONENTS (real exports), PROPS (typed), BEHAVIOR (events + routing), and ACCEPTANCE (definition of done). Pick any spec, the work is bounded and PR-shaped.
⌖ The wireframes are the visual target — build to them, not just to this prose.

Every load-bearing and net-new surface has been wireframed at the agreed northstar (Apple-grade ease; the Moves module is the bar) using the Source module's locked tokens. Where a spec links a wireframe, the wireframe is the contract for layout, hierarchy, spacing, and copy tone. This prose defines the data, files, props, and acceptance; the wireframe defines what it looks like.
  • 05-wireframe-atlas.html — the master reference. Cover, northstar, locked-token strip, a spec→surface→verdict index, and inline wireframes for Decision Queue (Spec 1), Intake footer (Spec 2), Approval page (Spec 3), Pricing/BAFO (Spec 11), Transition (Spec 13), Evidence drawer (Spec 16), Attention (Spec 18), plus schematic notes for the composed stages (Specs 9, 10, 14, 17). Start here.
  • 06-strategy-screen.html — full-fidelity Strategy stage. The pattern-setter for Specs 5, 6, 7, 8 (Next-Move card · proportional Sentinel rail · humanized shelf · export-gated). Every stage canvas matches this fidelity.
  • 07-executive-decision-screen.html — full-fidelity Executive Decision page-1. The fidelity bar for Spec 12 (1+3 dark-header verdict · one primary action · dissent first-class · squint-test-first).
Each spec below carries a ◧ WIREFRAME line pointing to its target. The design-module verdicts (approve / revise, and the 8 cross-spec answers) live in 04-design-module-review.md — read a spec's verdict before you build it; several specs were revised (e.g. Spec 3 collapses four buttons to one primary, Spec 7's humanization scope was widened, Spec 11's iceberg is stacked-bars-not-skeuomorphic).

PART 2The bar · design principles

Five principles. Every spec must clear all five.

  1. Lead with the answer, not the workings. Page 1 of every surface tells the CXO the decision/state. The reasoning is below the fold.
  2. Subtract before adding. Every visible element earns its place by changing what the user does next. If it doesn't, demote or delete.
  3. Match chrome to mental task. Drafting stages need chat; deciding stages need document focus; reviewing stages need evidence proximity.
  4. Internal taxonomy never leaks. Artifact codes, table names, scaffold tier labels — all hidden in production. Author-mode only.
  5. Honesty without paper cuts. Disclaimers and gap-flags appear when load-bearing, not as wallpaper. One persistent banner max.

The Apple test

For every page, blur the screenshot 50%. Can you still tell where the primary action is? If no, hierarchy is broken. If yes, ship it.

Triage banding logic (triage-banding.ts)
function bandFor(decision: SourceDecision): TriageBand {
  const daysToTrigger = differenceInDays(decision.triggerDate, now);
  if (daysToTrigger < 0) return 'OVERDUE';
  if (daysToTrigger <= 90) return 'DUE_THIS_QUARTER';
  return 'PIPELINE';
}

SPEC 4Lifecycle-state routing guard

Route by lifecycle_state · canvas physically blocked until approved
Refs Wireframe state machine · Closes Anand finding "canvas opens even when not approved"
NEWShi
Files
src/lib/source/lifecycle-routing-guard.ts src/app/(maestro)/source/events/[eventId]/page.tsx (add guard call at top) src/app/(maestro)/source/events/[eventId]/value/page.tsx (add guard call) src/proxy.ts (optional: middleware-level redirect for performance)
Routing rules
function resolveEventRoute(
  eventId: string,
  lifecycleState: SourceLifecycleState,
  requestedPath: string  // e.g. "?stage=strategy" or "/value" or "/approval"
): RouteAction {
  switch (lifecycleState) {
    case 'waiting_on_client':
    case 'waiting_on_co_approver':
    case 'draft_revision':
      // Block canvas. Allow only /approval.
      if (requestedPath.includes('/approval')) return { allow: true };
      return { redirect: `/source/events/${eventId}/approval` };

    case 'active':
      // Block /approval. Allow canvas + stages.
      if (requestedPath.includes('/approval')) {
        return { redirect: `/source/events/${eventId}?stage=current` };
      }
      return { allow: true };

    case 'closed':
    case 'closed_rejected':
      // Read-only summary view.
      return { redirect: `/source/events/${eventId}/summary` };

    case 'archived':
      return { redirect: `/source/queue` };
  }
}
Acceptance
  • Typing canvas URL directly when event is waiting_on_client → 302 to /approval
  • Typing /approval URL when event is active → 302 to canvas at current stage
  • Typing canvas URL when event is closed → 302 to /summary read-only view
  • Approval page redirect happens server-side (no flash of canvas)
  • Audit log entry on every redirect (route-attempt logging)
OPEN FOR DESIGN REVIEW:
  • Should the guard run in middleware (faster, no flash) or in the page component (cleaner, but brief flash possible)?
  • For closed events: separate /summary page (NEW) or read-only canvas view (modify existing)?
  • If user is mid-action when an event transitions (e.g., approver clicks Approve while another tab has canvas open) — invalidate the stale tab how? Toast + reload? Silent reload?

Sizing policy
function chatWidthForStage(stageKey: SourceStageKey): { widthPct: number; collapsed: boolean } {
  const map = {
    intake:              { widthPct: 50, collapsed: false },
    strategy:            { widthPct: 40, collapsed: false },
    scope:               { widthPct: 40, collapsed: false },
    rfp:                 { widthPct: 40, collapsed: false },
    responses:           { widthPct: 30, collapsed: false },
    evaluation:          { widthPct: 30, collapsed: false },
    pricing:             { widthPct: 35, collapsed: false },
    bafo:                { widthPct: 35, collapsed: false },
    executive_decision:  { widthPct: 15, collapsed: true },   // load-bearing
    selection:           { widthPct: 25, collapsed: false },
    transition:          { widthPct: 30, collapsed: false },
    value:               { widthPct: 25, collapsed: false },
  };
  return map[stageKey] ?? { widthPct: 40, collapsed: false };
}
Acceptance
  • Chat panel CSS width matches policy on stage mount
  • "collapsed" state shows compact stub: "Sentinel · Click to expand · 3 stage-specific suggestions"
  • User can override (toggle expand/collapse) but does NOT persist across stages (each stage opens at its policy default)
  • Suggestions are stage-aware (different prompts on Strategy vs BAFO)
  • Disclaimers compress to ONE line on collapsed state (not two stacked)
OPEN FOR DESIGN REVIEW:
  • Should user's manual collapse/expand preference persist per-stage or globally?
  • On Executive Decision (collapsed by default): should it auto-expand if the user asks a question, or stay collapsed and overlay?
  • Animation between widths — instant snap or smooth transition? Smooth feels nice but might lag.

PART 6Open questions for the design module

Cross-spec questions

Q1 · Voice and tone: The current product uses second-person directive ("Draft your strategy memo"). Should the redesigned product hold that voice across all surfaces, or shift to passive/system-narrator at decision points ("Strategy memo awaiting draft")?
Q2 · Density philosophy: The portfolio view (Spec anchor) is high-density and reads executive-grade. The intake / canvas pages have been lower-density. Should we lift density uniformly to portfolio level, or vary density by mental task?
Q3 · Sentinel chat positioning: Spec 6 makes chat proportional to stage. Is this the right axis, or should chat instead be modal (always-on overlay) with the canvas reflowing per stage?
Q4 · Approval routing UX: Spec 3 has Approve / Send to co-approver / Request changes / Reject as 4 separate buttons. Is this too much choice? Should it collapse to "Make a decision" with secondary modal?
Q5 · "Required to advance" vs "Gate" terminology: Spec 5 + 7 propose softening "GATE" to "Required to advance." Does the term "gate" have real signal in sourcing vocabulary that we'd be losing?
Q6 · Dark header on Executive Decision (Spec 12): The dark charcoal header is a strong visual moment but breaks the otherwise warm cream palette. Right call or jarring?
Q7 · Mobile responsiveness: Current product is desktop-first. The wireframes don't address mobile. CXOs increasingly review on phones. Should mobile be a Wave 5 separate exercise, or built into every spec from start?
Q8 · Empty states: Specs reference "zero state" copy but don't spec them in detail. Should we author empty-state designs for every surface as part of this redesign?

Design module workflow ask

For each spec, leave a comment block at the bottom: 
// DESIGN MODULE REVIEW
// Approved as-is: [Y/N]
// Revisions:
//   - [bullet]
// Open with Codex before ship: [yes/no]
That structure makes the handoff to Codex deterministic.
